questions.explanation: Luke 6:31 presents the well-known golden rule: 'Do unto others as you would have them do unto you,' summarizing Jesus' teaching on practical kindness.

questions.text: What is Jesus’ instruction about judging others in Luke 6?
options: Do not judge, and you will not be judged
Judge others fairly but with mercy
Only judge those who break the law
questions.explanation: Luke 6:37 advises against judging others unfairly, stating that the measure you use will be measured to you.

questions.text: What comparison does Jesus use in Luke 6 to illustrate the importance of self-awareness?
options: A log in your own eye versus a speck in another's
A house built on a rock versus sand
A lamp on a stand versus under a basket
questions.explanation: Luke 6:41-42 contains Jesus' teaching about noticing the beam in one's own eye before pointing out the speck in another's, emphasizing self-awareness and humility.

questions.text: What was the centurion requesting from Jesus in Luke 7:3?
questions.explanation: The centurion sent elders to ask Jesus to heal his servant, as noted in Luke 7:3.

questions.text: How did Jesus respond to the centurion’s faith in Luke 7:9?
options: He commended the faith as great
questions.explanation: Jesus marveled at the centurion's faith, saying He had not found such faith even in Israel (Luke 7:9).

questions.text: What miracle did Jesus perform for the widow in Luke 7:11-15?
options: Raised her son from the dead
questions.explanation: Jesus raised the widow’s son from the dead at Nain, as described in Luke 7:11-15.

questions.text: What was Jesus' response to the woman’s grief at the funeral in Luke 7:13?
questions.explanation: Jesus saw her grief and was moved with compassion, which led to Him raising her son (Luke 7:13).

questions.text: What does Luke 7:24 say Jesus did in response to the crowd's questions about John the Baptist?
options: He explained the significance of John
questions.explanation: Jesus explained to the crowd the significance of John’s ministry, emphasizing his role and greatness (Luke 7:24-25).

questions.text: How did Jesus describe John the Baptist in Luke 7:28?
options: The Elijah who was to come
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that John was the greatest among those born of women, emphasizing his special role (Luke 7:28).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about those who listen to John’s message in Luke 7:29?
questions.explanation: Jesus said that those who heard and accepted God's word through John are blessed (Luke 7:29).

questions.text: What is the main theme of Luke 7?
questions.explanation: Luke 7 highlights faith, miracles, and the recognition of Jesus' authority through the actions and responses of individuals, such as the centurion and the widow’s son.

questions.text: Where does Jesus begin His ministry as described in Luke 8?
options: Teaching near the Sea of Galilee
questions.explanation: In Luke 8:1, Jesus is described as traveling from town to town, preaching and bringing the good news of the kingdom of God near the Sea of Galilee.

questions.text: Who is mentioned as supporting Jesus' ministry in Luke 8?
questions.explanation: Luke 8:3 mentions Joanna as one of the women supporting Jesus and the apostles, along with others like Mary Magdalene and Susanna.

questions.text: What type of soil does Jesus describe in the parable of the sower?
questions.explanation: In Luke 8:15, Jesus explains that the seed falling on good soil represents those who hear the word and retain it, yielding fruit.

questions.text: What was the reaction of the demon-possessed man after Jesus cast out the demons?
options: He was healed and stayed silent
He was restored to his family
questions.explanation: Luke 8:38-39 records that the man, after being healed, asked to follow Jesus but was instructed to share what God had done for him instead.

questions.text: What miracle does Jesus perform on the woman with a bleeding condition?
options: He asks her to touch His cloak
questions.explanation: In Luke 8:44, Jesus tells the woman that her faith has healed her after she touches His cloak, and her bleeding stops.

questions.text: How does Jesus demonstrate power over nature in Luke 8?
questions.explanation: Luke 8:22-25 describes Jesus calming a storm on the sea, demonstrating His authority over natural elements.

questions.text: What is the message Jesus gives about His family in Luke 8?
options: Those who listen to His teachings
Those who believe in His identity
questions.explanation: In Luke 8:21, Jesus states that His true family is those who hear God's word and do it, emphasizing spiritual kinship.

questions.text: What event prompts Jesus to ask, 'Who is my mother and my brothers?'?
options: When His family comes to see Him
After healing a man with a demon
questions.explanation: Luke 8:19-21 recounts that Jesus' mother and brothers come to see Him, but He responds by redefining His true family as those who hear God's word.

questions.text: What did Jesus give the twelve disciples authority over in Luke 9:1?
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:1, Jesus gave the disciples power and authority to heal and to cast out demons.

questions.text: Where did Jesus send the twelve disciples in Luke 9:3?
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:3, Jesus instructed the disciples to go to every town or village they entered, carrying no extra provisions.

questions.text: What instructions did Jesus give regarding possessions to those he sent out in Luke 9?
options: Take nothing and rely on hospitality
questions.explanation: Luke 9:3 emphasizes that Jesus sent the disciples with no staff, bag, bread, or money, depending on God's provision and hospitality.

questions.text: What was Jesus' instruction about whom to stay with in Luke 9:4?
options: Stay in the same house until you leave town
Avoid staying in one place too long
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed them to stay in one house and not move around from one place to another while in that town (Luke 9:4).

questions.text: How did Jesus respond when the disciples wanted to call down fire on a Samaritan village in Luke 9:54?
options: He rebuked them for their anger
He agreed and prayed for fire
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:55-56, Jesus rebuked the disciples, telling them to keep their focus on the mission and not seek revenge or destruction.

questions.text: What does Jesus say about losing life for His sake in Luke 9:24?
options: Losing life for Jesus' sake leads to salvation
Losing life means giving up all possessions
Losing life is not mentioned in this chapter
questions.explanation: Luke 9:24 explains that those who try to save their lives will lose them, but those who lose their lives for Christ will save them.

questions.text: What does Peter, James, and John see during the Transfiguration in Luke 9:29?
options: Jesus' face and clothing become radiant
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:29, Jesus' appearance changes and his clothing becomes dazzling, shining like lightning during the Transfiguration.

questions.text: What do Peter, James, and John see after the Transfiguration in Luke 9:31?
options: Moses and Elijah conversing with Jesus
questions.explanation: Luke 9:30-31 records that Moses and Elijah appeared and talked with Jesus about his upcoming departure, revealing their significance in God's plan.

questions.text: Who is the speaker in Malachi 1?
questions.explanation: Malachi 1:1 indicates that the oracle is from the Lord to Israel through the prophet Malachi.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of Malachi 1:1?
options: To declare God's love for Israel
questions.explanation: Malachi 1:1 states that the message is about God's love for Israel, which is the central theme of the chapter.

questions.text: How does God describe His love for Jacob in Malachi 1:2?
options: He loved him from the beginning
He loved Jacob and hated Esau
He blessed him with many descendants
questions.explanation: Malachi 1:2 states, 'I have loved Jacob, but Esau I have hated,' highlighting God's special love for Jacob over Esau.

questions.text: What negative attitude do the priests display in Malachi 1:6-7?
questions.explanation: Malachi 1:6-7 speaks of the priests dishonoring God's name by offering polluted sacrifices and disrespecting His altar.

questions.text: What has God accused the priests of in Malachi 1:8?
questions.explanation: Malachi 1:8 criticizes the priests for presenting lame and sick animals as sacrifices instead of the proper offerings.

questions.text: What does God say about His name among the nations in Malachi 1:11?
questions.explanation: Malachi 1:11 affirms that God's name is great among the nations, indicating His universal reputation.

questions.text: What attitude does God rebuke in Malachi 1:14 regarding sacrifices?
questions.explanation: Malachi 1:14 rebukes the attitude of giving blemished sacrifices, calling it a 'defiling' act and describing it as evil in God's sight.

questions.text: What does Malachi 1 emphasize about God's view of acceptable worship?
options: God requires pure and sincere offerings
questions.explanation: Malachi 1 reveals that God values sincere and unblemished offerings, and rejects offerings that are defective or disrespectful.

questions.text: What warning does Malachi give to the priests in Malachi 2:1?
options: To repent and seek God's favor
To listen and pay attention to the law
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:1 warns the priests to pay attention and listen because of their failure to honor God's name and the covenant.

questions.text: What did the priests do that was considered a major offense in Malachi 2:8?
options: They compromised the Law and led many astray
They refused to serve in the temple
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:8 criticizes the priests for turning from the way and causing many to stumble by changing the law, thus compromising their spiritual leadership.

questions.text: What does Malachi accuse the priests of doing in relation to God's covenant in Malachi 2:5?
options: Walking with God in peace and uprightness
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:5 states that the priests' covenant with God was faithfulness and reverence, which they are failing to uphold.

questions.text: Malachi 2:10 asks a question about God's people. What is the question?
options: Will God accept worship from us?
Has one God created us all?
Will God not judge the earth?
Is there no one righteous among us?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:10 asks if God has not made them one, emphasizing God's unity and their collective responsibility in faithfulness.

questions.text: What does Malachi emphasize about the Lord in Malachi 2:11?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:11 highlights that the Lord detests divorce and faithless practices, calling His people to faithfulness.

questions.text: In Malachi 2:16, what does God say about those who are unfaithful in marriage?
options: He hates divorce and covering wounds
He is indifferent to marriage issues
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:16 clearly states that God hates divorce and covering wounds, emphasizing His desire for faithfulness in marriage.

questions.text: What overarching theme can be seen in Malachi 2 regarding God's expectations?
options: Legal rituals must be performed properly
Religious leaders should live in wealth
Fasting is more important than justice
questions.explanation: Malachi 2 emphasizes God's desire for faithful worship, honesty, and faithfulness in relationships, particularly in the context of the priesthood and marriage.

questions.text: Who does Malachi mention as being sent to prepare the way for the Lord?
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:1 mentions a messenger sent to prepare the way before the Lord, often understood as a prophetic reference to John the Baptist or the coming messenger.

questions.text: According to Malachi 3, how will the messenger prepare the people for God's arrival?
options: By turning hearts back to God
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:1-2 speaks of the messenger turning the hearts of the fathers to their children and vice versa, preparing a people who are righteous for God's coming.

questions.text: What benefit does God promise to those who fear Him and honor His name in Malachi 3?
options: They will be blessed with abundance
They will have their names written in Heaven
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:16-17 describes how God preserves those who fear Him, and they will be His treasured possession, spared from punishment.

questions.text: What action does God challenge people to do regarding their tithes and offerings?
options: Bring the full tithe into the storehouse
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:8-10 clearly calls on the people to bring the full tithe into the storehouse so that there will be food in God's house.

questions.text: What does God say will happen if people do not bring the tithes and offerings?
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:9 states that God will curse the devourer for their sakes if they do not bring tithes and offerings, highlighting the importance of obedience in stewardship.

questions.text: Which phrase describes God's promise to those who serve Him faithfully in Malachi 3?
options: He will open the windows of Heaven
He will make their enemies flee
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:10 promises that God will open the windows of Heaven and pour out a blessing until it overflows for those who serve Him faithfully.

questions.text: In Malachi 3, how is the Lord described in relation to His coming?
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:2 describes the Lord as a refiner and purifier, emphasizing His role in cleansing and refining His people in preparation for His coming.

questions.text: What is the role of Elijah as described in Malachi 4:5-6?
options: To restore hearts and turn people to God
questions.explanation: Malachi 4:5-6 states Elijah will come before the great and dreadful day to turn hearts of parents to children and vice versa, emphasizing spiritual renewal.

questions.text: What does the opening of Matthew 1 primarily focus on?
options: The birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
questions.explanation: Matthew 1 begins with the genealogy of Jesus, tracing his lineage from Abraham to David and through generations, establishing his royal and Jewish heritage (Matthew 1:1-17).

questions.text: Which ancestor is NOT mentioned in Matthew 1:1-17?
questions.explanation: Joseph is mentioned as the husband of Mary and in Jesus' legal lineage, but he is not listed as an ancestor in the genealogy itself in Matthew 1:1-17.

questions.text: Which woman is specifically named as part of Jesus' genealogy?
questions.explanation: Rahab is mentioned in Matthew 1:5 as an ancestor in Jesus' lineage, demonstrating God's grace throughout family histories.

questions.text: What is significant about the lineage listed in Matthew 1:1–17?
options: It emphasizes Jesus' royal and legal descent
It shows Jesus' connection to pagan nations
It focuses on Jesus' spiritual talents
questions.explanation: Matthew's genealogy emphasizes Jesus' royal and legal descent through Joseph, highlighting his royal Davidic lineage (Matthew 1:1-17).

questions.text: Which of these is mentioned as a father of a king in Matthew 1?
questions.explanation: Solomon is listed as a son of David, emphasizing the royal lineage leading to Jesus (Matthew 1:6).

questions.text: Which biblical figure is NOT included in Matthew's genealogy in chapter 1?
questions.explanation: Abel is not mentioned in the genealogy; rather, Matthew includes Tamar, Rahab, and Bathsheba who are listed as ancestors (Matthew 1:3-6).

questions.text: What is the main purpose of Matthew 1's genealogy?
options: To establish Jesus' legal and royal lineage
questions.explanation: The genealogy in Matthew 1 aims to establish Jesus' legal right to the throne of David, confirming his messianic credentials (Matthew 1:1-17).

questions.text: Who summoned the twelve disciples in Matthew 10?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 10:1, Jesus calls his twelve disciples to him and gives them authority.

questions.text: What authority does Jesus give to His disciples in this chapter?
options: Authority to perform miracles only at the temple
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:1 states that Jesus gave His disciples authority to cast out unclean spirits and heal every disease.

questions.text: Which of the following was NOT one of the instructions Jesus gave to the disciples?
options: Preach that the kingdom of heaven has come near
questions.explanation: In Matthew 10:9-10, Jesus instructs them not to take gold or silver, but to rely on God's provision and focus on preaching and healing.

questions.text: How should the disciples regard those who welcome or reject them?
options: Treat the house as worthy if they listen
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:11-13 indicates that disciples should respect hospitality and if rejected, shake off the dust as a testimony, but treat those who welcome them as worthy.

questions.text: What warning does Jesus give about persecution?
options: Persecution will be rare and unimportant
Disciples will face opposition from family and authorities
Disciples will not face any persecution
questions.explanation: In Matthew 10:16-22, Jesus warns that His disciples will face persecution, even from family, and must endure faithfully.

questions.text: What does Jesus say about fearing those who persecute you?
options: Fear them because they control your life
Fear only God, who can destroy both body and soul
Fear no one, for persecution is rare
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:28 states that believers should fear God, who has authority over life and death, rather than human persecutors.

questions.text: What promise does Jesus make to those who receive His messengers?
options: They will inherit eternal life and receive a reward
questions.explanation: In Matthew 10:40-42, Jesus says that welcoming His disciples is akin to welcoming Him and that such acts of hospitality will be rewarded.

questions.text: Who did Jesus send to question John the Baptist about his deeds?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:2-3, Jesus' disciples are sent to ask John if He is the one to come. This highlights Jesus' relationship with His followers and their questions about His identity.

questions.text: What was Jesus' response to John's disciples about the deeds they saw?
options: The blind see, the lame walk
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:4-5, Jesus responds by citing the miracles performed—blind seeing, lame walking, lepers being cleansed—affirming His messianic work as fulfillment of prophecy.

questions.text: How does Jesus describe the towns that rejected His miracle work?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:20-24, Jesus condemns Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum for their lack of repentance despite witnessing His deeds, calling them unrepentant towns.

questions.text: What did Jesus say about those who are weary and burdened?
options: They will find rest in Him
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:28-30, Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come to Him for rest, emphasizing His gentle and humble heart.

questions.text: What did Jesus say about the unrepentant generation's response to His message?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:16-19, Jesus criticizes the generation for rejecting both John’s asceticism and His own ministry, showing their unrepentant attitude.

questions.text: What did Jesus say about the wisdom of God in relation to children’s responses?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:25-26, Jesus prays, acknowledging that the Father has hidden wisdom from the wise and revealed it to infants, highlighting divine revelation.

questions.text: What does Jesus say about coming to Him and learning from Him?
options: You will find rest for your souls
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:28-29, Jesus invites all who are weary to come to Him and learn from Him, promising rest for their souls through His gentle and humble heart.

questions.text: What invitation does Jesus extend to those who are burdened?
options: Come to me, and I will give you rest
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:28, Jesus warmly invites the weary and burdened to come to Him for rest, emphasizing His role as the source of relief and peace.

questions.text: Why did Jesus' disciples pick grain on the Sabbath in Matthew 12:1-2?
questions.explanation: Jesus' disciples picked grain because they were hungry, which the Pharisees questioned regarding Sabbath rules (Matthew 12:1-2).

questions.text: How did Jesus respond to the Pharisees accusing His disciples of breaking the Sabbath?
options: He agreed with their strict rules
He said the Sabbath was made for man
questions.explanation: Jesus explained that 'The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath,' emphasizing the purpose of Sabbath rest (Matthew 12:6-8).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about the Lord of the Sabbath in Matthew 12:8?
options: He is the Son of man
He is Lord of the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Jesus declared that He is Lord of the Sabbath, asserting His authority over the Sabbath laws (Matthew 12:8).

questions.text: Why did Jesus heal the man's withered hand on the Sabbath in Matthew 12:9-13?
options: To make a statement about work
questions.explanation: Jesus healed the man to demonstrate compassion and that doing good is lawful on the Sabbath (Matthew 12:13).

questions.text: What did the Pharisees plan after Jesus healed the man with the withered hand?
options: To find a way to kill Him
questions.explanation: The Pharisees conspired to destroy Jesus because they saw His healings and actions as violations of their rules (Matthew 12:14).

questions.text: What did Jesus warn about the accusation against Him in Matthew 12:24-25?
options: That every kingdom divided will fall
questions.explanation: Jesus warned that a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand, illustrating the foolishness of accusing Him of driving out demons by Satan's power (Matthew 12:25).

questions.text: What is the significance of the 'blasphemy against the Spirit' mentioned in Matthew 12:31-32?
options: It is the ultimate rejection of Jesus
It is a sin of the tongue
questions.explanation: Jesus states that blasphemy against the Spirit is unforgivable because it signifies complete rejection of the Holy Spirit's work and Jesus' divine ministry (Matthew 12:31-32).

questions.text: What does Jesus teach about signs in Matthew 12:38-39?
options: A wicked and adulterous generation seeks a sign
questions.explanation: Jesus indicates that seeking signs as a test is a sign of unbelief, and He calls the generation wicked and adulterous in their demand for a sign (Matthew 12:39).

questions.text: What is the main setting for the parable in Matthew 13?
questions.explanation: Jesus taught the parables by the Sea of Galilee, as described in Matthew 13:1-2.

questions.text: What does the parable of the sower primarily illustrate?
questions.explanation: The parable explains how different types of soil represent various responses to the seed (God's word), as explained in Matthew 13:3-9, 18-23.

questions.text: Which type of soil represents those who hear the word but fall away due to persecution or troubles?
questions.explanation: Stony soil depicts those who quickly receive the word but stumble when faced with persecution or affliction, as described in Matthew 13:20-21.

questions.text: What is the 'mustard seed' a metaphor for in Matthew 13?
options: The Kingdom of Heaven grows from small beginnings
questions.explanation: The mustard seed illustrates how the Kingdom of Heaven starts small but becomes large, filling the whole field (Matthew 13:31-32).

questions.text: In the parable of the wheat and the weeds, who is responsible for sowing the weeds?
questions.explanation: The enemy sowed weeds among the wheat, as explained in Matthew 13:25-28, symbolizing opposition to God's work.

questions.text: What is the purpose of Jesus teaching in parables in Matthew 13?
options: To hide the truth from others
To reveal truths to those open to understanding
questions.explanation: Jesus used parables to reveal truths about the Kingdom of Heaven to those willing to listen and understand, as indicated in Matthew 13:10-17.

questions.text: What does Jesus suggest about those who hear the parables but do not understand?
options: The knowledge is hidden from them
questions.explanation: Jesus indicates that the secrets of the Kingdom are hidden from those who do not understand, as discussed in Matthew 13:11-12.

questions.text: How are the values in the parables of Matthew 13 meant to influence believers?
options: Encourage seeking understanding of God's kingdom
questions.explanation: The parables highlight the importance of understanding and valuing the Kingdom of Heaven, encouraging believers to seek deeper insight, as seen throughout the chapter.

questions.text: Who was the ruler that heard about Jesus and had John the Baptist beheaded?
questions.explanation: King Herod heard about Jesus and ordered the beheading of John the Baptist, as described in Matthew 14:1-10.

questions.text: What did Jesus do when he saw the large crowd in Matthew 14?
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:14 states that Jesus had compassion on the crowd and healed their sick.

questions.text: How many loaves and fish did the boy have that Jesus used to feed the crowd?
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:17 indicates the boy had five loaves and two fish, which Jesus blessed and multiplied to feed thousands.

questions.text: What did Peter do when he saw Jesus walking on the water?
options: He got out of the boat to walk to Jesus
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:29-30 recounts Peter stepping out of the boat and walking toward Jesus, but he then began to sink.

questions.text: What was King Herod’s reaction to hearing about Jesus after John the Baptist's death?
options: He was confused and thought Jesus was John
He believed Jesus was the Messiah
He sent soldiers to find Jesus
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:1-2 explains Herod's confusion, thinking Jesus might be John the Baptist risen from the dead.

questions.text: After the miracle of feeding the 5000, what did Jesus tell the disciples to do?
options: Go to the mountain to pray
Get into the boat and go ahead of Him
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:22-23 notes Jesus telling the disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of Him to the other side.

questions.text: What was Peter’s response when Jesus invited him to walk on the water?
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:28-29 describes Peter asking to walk on the water and stepping out in faith, though he began to sink when he doubted.

questions.text: What did Jesus do after feeding the 5000 with five loaves and two fish?
options: He sent the disciples ahead in the boat
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:22 mentions Jesus telling the disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of Him to the other side while He dismissed the crowd.

questions.text: Why did the Pharisees and scribes criticize Jesus' disciples in Matthew 15?
options: They did not wash their hands before eating
They ate food with unclean hands
questions.explanation: The Pharisees and scribes accused the disciples of violating the tradition of washing hands before eating (Matthew 15:2), which Jesus addresses as a matter of tradition rather than God's commandments.

questions.text: What does Jesus say defiles a person in Matthew 15?
options: What comes out of the mouth
questions.explanation: Jesus responds that evil intentions and words that originate from the heart, which come out of the mouth, defile a person, emphasizing spiritual purity over ritual cleanliness (Matthew 15:11).

questions.text: How did Jesus respond to the disciples' concern about the crowd being hungry?
options: He told them to buy food
He performed the miracle of feeding 4,000
questions.explanation: Jesus performed the miracle of feeding the four thousand with seven loaves and a few fish, showing compassion and divine provision (Matthew 15:32-38).

questions.text: What was the main reason Jesus criticized the Pharisees and scribes?
options: They rejected Him as the Messiah
They emphasized human traditions over God's commandments
They refused to heal the sick
questions.explanation: Jesus rebuked them for setting aside God's commandments in favor of human traditions, highlighting their hypocrisy and neglect of God's true commands (Matthew 15:3-9).

questions.text: What does Jesus say about what comes out of the heart in Matthew 15?
options: It is only influenced by the environment
questions.explanation: Jesus explains that evil thoughts and evil actions originate from the heart, which defile a person, emphasizing internal moral purity (Matthew 15:18-19).

questions.text: Who came to Jesus asking for help in Matthew 15?
questions.explanation: A Canaanite woman approached Jesus seeking healing for her daughter, demonstrating faith despite cultural barriers (Matthew 15:22).

questions.text: What was Jesus' response to the woman who asked for her daughter's healing?
options: He said it was not right to take children's bread and give it to dogs
He told her to pray more
He told her to come back later
questions.explanation: Jesus initially replied that it was not right to take the children's bread and toss it to dogs, but He ultimately healed her faith, demonstrating perseverance and faith (Matthew 15:26-28).

questions.text: What did the Pharisees and Sadducees ask Jesus to show them?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 16:1, the Pharisees and Sadducees asked Jesus to show them a sign from heaven to test Him.

questions.text: How did Jesus respond to the request for a sign from heaven?
options: He pointed to His previous miracles
He attributed it to their faith
questions.explanation: Jesus rebuked the Pharisees and Sadducees, saying they could not interpret the signs of the times and refused to give them a sign from heaven (Matthew 16:4).

questions.text: Who was present with Jesus during the Transfiguration according to Matthew 17?
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:3-4 mentions Moses and Elijah appearing alongside Jesus during the Transfiguration.

questions.text: What was Jesus' appearance like during the Transfiguration?
options: His face shone like the sun
He looked like a regular man
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:2 describes Jesus' face shining like the sun during the Transfiguration.

questions.text: How did the disciples react to the Transfiguration event?
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:6 indicates the disciples were afraid and fell facedown when they saw Jesus' glory.

questions.text: What command did Jesus give to the disciples after the Transfiguration when they questioned what it meant?
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:9 records Jesus instructing them to tell no one until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.

questions.text: Why did Peter suggest building three tabernacles during the Transfiguration incident?
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:4 shows Peter's impulsive idea to build tabernacles for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah, perhaps to honor them or prolong the experience.

questions.text: What was Elijah's role in the Transfiguration event?
options: He appeared and talked with Jesus
He was seen ascending to heaven
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:3 notes Elijah appeared and was talking with Jesus during the Transfiguration.

questions.text: How did the voice from heaven describe Jesus during the Transfiguration?
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:5 records God's voice proclaiming Jesus as His beloved Son with whom He is well pleased.

questions.text: What was the disciples' main concern after witnessing the Transfiguration?
options: What it meant for the Law
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:9-10 shows the disciples questioned Jesus about the meaning of His glory and Elijah's return, indicating their curiosity about its significance.

questions.text: Who among the disciples argued about greatness in Matthew 18?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 18:1, the disciples approached Jesus asking who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

questions.text: What does Jesus do to demonstrate humility in Matthew 18?
options: He calls a child to stand among them
questions.explanation: In Matthew 18:2-4, Jesus calls a child and uses him as a model to teach humility, stating that unless one becomes like a child, they cannot enter the kingdom of heaven.

questions.text: What should be done if a brother sins against you according to Matthew 18?
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:15 advises to privately confront the brother who sinned against you to seek reconciliation.

questions.text: What is Jesus’ instruction if a brother refuses to listen after the first confrontation?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 18:15-17, Jesus teaches that if a brother refuses to listen after private correction, one should take it to the church for further steps.

questions.text: What example does Jesus use to describe how often one should forgive a brother in Matthew 18?
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:22 records Jesus telling Peter to forgive 'seventy times seven' times, illustrating unlimited forgiveness.

questions.text: What is the significance of the parable of the lost sheep in Matthew 18?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 18:12-14, Jesus emphasizes that God actively seeks out the lost sheep, highlighting God's compassion and effort to save sinners.

questions.text: What is Jesus’ assurance to the one who has gone astray and is forgiven?
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:13-14 states that when a lost sheep is found and forgiven, there is great rejoicing in heaven, indicating God's joy over repentance.

questions.text: Where does Jesus go after His conversation in Matthew 19?
options: To the region of Judea beyond the Jordan
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:1 states Jesus leaves Judea and crosses the Jordan to the region beyond, indicating His movement after teaching.

questions.text: What question do the Pharisees ask Jesus in Matthew 19?
options: Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?
How can one attain eternal life?
questions.explanation: The Pharisees asked Jesus about the lawfulness of divorce, as recorded in Matthew 19:3.

questions.text: How does Jesus describe the beginning of creation regarding marriage?
options: Male and female He created them
questions.explanation: Jesus refers to Genesis, stating that from the beginning, God made male and female, establishing the divine origin of marriage (Matthew 19:4-5).

questions.text: What reason does Jesus give for the exception in divorce?
questions.explanation: Jesus explains that Moses permitted divorce due to people's hardness of heart, but it was not part of God's original plan (Matthew 19:8).

questions.text: What do Jesus' disciples say about Jesus’ teaching on divorce?
options: It is better not to marry
It is better to follow Moses
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle
questions.explanation: The disciples express that Jesus' teaching on marriage and divorce is hard to accept, implying the seriousness of His words (Matthew 19:10).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about children and the kingdom of heaven?
options: Children are not important in faith
The kingdom belongs to the wise
Let the little children come to Me
Children must be perfect to enter
questions.explanation: Jesus welcomes children and says, ‘Let the little children come to Me,’ highlighting their importance in the kingdom (Matthew 19:14).

questions.text: What does Jesus say about the reward for those who leave everything for Him?
options: They will be equal to angels
questions.explanation: Jesus assures that anyone who leaves family or possessions for His sake will receive a hundredfold and inherit eternal life (Matthew 19:29).

questions.text: What is Jesus' teaching about the first and the last in Matthew 19?
options: The last will be first, and the first last
The first are the greatest in the kingdom
The last are the least in God's eyes
questions.explanation: Jesus concludes with the statement that the last will be first, and the first last, emphasizing humility in the kingdom (Matthew 19:30).

questions.text: In Matthew 2, who visits Jesus after His birth?
questions.explanation: Matthew 2 describes wise men coming from the East to worship Jesus (verse 1-2).

questions.text: What was the main purpose of the wise men’s visit?
options: To offer gifts and worship Jesus
To deliver a message from the king
questions.explanation: The wise men came to worship Jesus and offer gifts, as stated in verses 10-11.

questions.text: How did King Herod react when he heard about Jesus' birth?
questions.explanation: Herod was troubled and disturbed when he learned from the wise men about the newborn King (verse 3).

questions.text: What was Herod’s plan after learning about the child?
questions.explanation: Herod secretly plotted to kill Jesus to eliminate any threat to his throne (verses 13-16).

questions.text: Where did Joseph, Mary, and Jesus go after fleeing Herod?
questions.explanation: Joseph was warned in a dream to escape to Egypt with Mary and Jesus, fulfilling prophecy (verse 13-15).

questions.text: What prophecy did Matthew say was fulfilled by Jesus’ return from Egypt?
options: Out of Egypt I called My Son
questions.explanation: Matthew quotes Hosea 11:1 to show Jesus' return from Egypt fulfilled this prophecy (verse 15).

questions.text: How did King Herod react upon realizing the wise men outwitted him?
options: He was furious and ordered the massacre of infants
He sought another way to find Jesus
questions.explanation: Herod’s anger led to the mass killing of male children in Bethlehem, as described in verses 16-18.

questions.text: What gift did the wise men bring to Jesus?
questions.explanation: The wise men presented gold, frankincense, and myrrh, as noted in verse 11.

questions.text: What is the parable Jesus tells in Matthew 20 about workers in a vineyard?
options: Workers hired at different times receive different pay
Workers hired at different times receive the same pay
Workers who work early are rewarded more
Workers refuse to work for the vineyard owner
questions.explanation: In Matthew 20:1-16, Jesus explains that all workers hired, regardless of when they start, receive the same pay—denoting God's graciousness and generosity.

questions.text: What does the landowner compare the pay to in the parable?
options: A fair wage for work done
A gift, like what he chooses to give
A salary based on hours worked
questions.explanation: In verse 15, the landowner emphasizes his right to do what he wishes with his own money, illustrating God's sovereign grace and generosity.

questions.text: How do the workers hired early respond when they see others receive what they were promised?
questions.explanation: In verses 11-12, the early workers grumble, feeling they deserve more because they worked longer, but the landowner’s generosity is the focus of the parable.

questions.text: What is Jesus' main teaching through this parable?
options: God’s grace is generous and sovereign
Workers should be content with less
The early workers are more faithful
questions.explanation: The parable illustrates that God's grace extends equally to all, and His generosity is not based on human notions of fairness, as explained in verses 15-16.

questions.text: Who do the workers represent in the parable?
questions.explanation: The workers symbolize people, especially those invited into God's kingdom at different times, emphasizing divine grace freely given to all who respond.

questions.text: What does Jesus say about the first and last in the kingdom of heaven?
options: The first will be last, and the last will be first
The first are honored by God
The first will receive special blessings
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches in verses 16 that many who are considered last will be first, and vice versa, highlighting God's reverse kingdom principles based on grace.

questions.text: What is Peter’s question to Jesus regarding reward in Matthew 20?
options: What shall we have for following you?
Who is the greatest in the kingdom?
questions.explanation: In verse 27, Peter asks about their reward, prompting Jesus to teach about service and greatness in the kingdom, emphasizing that true reward is based on humility and service.

questions.text: What did Jesus predict about His coming in Matthew 20?
options: He will set up an earthly kingdom
He will suffer and be rejected
He will return victorious on a cloud
He will establish law and order
questions.explanation: Verses 17-19 describe Jesus predicting His suffering, death, and resurrection, which is the fulfillment of God's plan for salvation.

questions.text: What did Jesus instruct His disciples to do as He approached Jerusalem?
options: To bring a donkey and colt
questions.explanation: Jesus told His disciples to find a donkey with her colt and bring them to Him, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy (Matthew 21:2-3).

questions.text: How did the crowd react when Jesus entered Jerusalem?
options: They welcomed Him with shouts of praise
questions.explanation: The crowd spread their cloaks and branches on the road, shouting 'Hosanna' and praising Jesus as he entered Jerusalem (Matthew 21:8-9).

questions.text: What did Jesus do when He entered the temple?
options: He drove out those selling and buying
questions.explanation: Jesus overturned the tables of the money changers and those selling doves, expressing anger that the temple had become a house of trade (Matthew 21:12-13).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about the barren fig tree?
options: It will never bear fruit again
It has already borne much fruit
It will be destroyed by fire
questions.explanation: Jesus cursed the fig tree for not bearing fruit, and it withered, symbolizing judgment (Matthew 21:19-21).

questions.text: What authority did Jesus challenge the religious leaders about?
options: Their authority to cleanse the temple
questions.explanation: Jesus questioned by what authority He was acting, especially regarding cleansing the temple, and challenged their authority (Matthew 21:23-27).

questions.text: How did Jesus describe the guests invited to the king’s banquet?
options: They were excited and came early
questions.explanation: Jesus told the parable of the wedding banquet, where invitees made excuses and declined the king's invitation (Matthew 22:3-5).

questions.text: What lesson did Jesus teach with the parable of the tenants?
options: Rejection of God's messengers and Son
questions.explanation: Jesus told the parable illustrating how the landowner’s tenants rejected and persecuted his servants and son, symbolizing Israel’s rejection of prophets and Jesus (Matthew 21:33-39).

questions.text: What was Jesus’ response when the religious leaders questioned His authority?
options: He told a parable about a lost sheep
He asked about John’s baptism and its authority
questions.explanation: Jesus responded by questioning their authority, asking whether John’s baptism was from heaven or human, exposing their unwillingness to answer (Matthew 21:23-27).

questions.text: What type of event is described in Matthew 22:1-2?
questions.explanation: Matthew 22:1-2 describes the kingdom of heaven as being like a wedding feast for the king's son, illustrating the imagery of a wedding banquet.

questions.text: How did the invited guests initially respond to the wedding invitation?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 22:3-5, many invitees declined the invitation or paid no attention, with some going back to their work or affairs.

questions.text: What was the response of the king upon receiving news that some guests refused to come?
options: He sent servants to invite others
questions.explanation: Matthew 22:4-6 describes how the king sent his servants to invite others—both good and bad—to fill the wedding hall, showing God's extending of His invitation.

questions.text: What is the significance of the wedding garment mentioned in Matthew 22:11-12?
options: It signifies readiness for the feast
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 highlight that the wedding garment signifies proper preparation and righteousness necessary to partake in the kingdom of heaven.

questions.text: What was the main message of the Parable of the Wedding Feast?
options: God’s invitation is open to all
questions.explanation: The parable emphasizes that God’s invitation to His kingdom is extended to everyone, but there is a need for proper preparation and acceptance.

questions.text: How does Matthew 22:15-17 describe the religious leaders' attempt to trap Jesus?
options: They asked about the greatest commandment
questions.explanation: In verses 15-17, the Pharisees and Herodians ask Jesus whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, trying to trap Him with a difficult question.

questions.text: What was Jesus' response to the question about paying taxes in Matthew 22:21?
questions.explanation: Jesus instructs to 'Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s,' indicating the importance of respecting civic authorities (Matthew 22:21).

questions.text: What commandment does Jesus identify as the greatest in Matthew 22:37-39?
questions.explanation: Verses 37-39 record Jesus affirming that the greatest commandments are to love God and to love your neighbor as yourself.

questions.text: Who did Jesus criticize for placing heavy burdens on others without helping to carry them?
questions.explanation: Jesus rebukes the scribes and Pharisees for putting burdens on people that they themselves do not lift with their own hands (Matthew 23:4).

questions.text: What does Jesus call the scribes and Pharisees in Matthew 23:13?
questions.explanation: Jesus refers to the scribes and Pharisees as hypocrites, criticizing their outward piety that hides inward corruption (Matthew 23:13).

questions.text: What phrase does Jesus often use to describe the leaders’ actions in Matthew 23?
questions.explanation: Jesus describes the Pharisees as 'whitewashed tombs,' appearing beautiful outwardly but inwardly full of hypocrisy and wickedness (Matthew 23:27-28).

questions.text: According to Jesus in Matthew 23, how do the Pharisees seek honor from others?
questions.explanation: Jesus notes that the Pharisees love to have titles and be greeted with respect in public to seek honor from others (Matthew 23:7-12).

questions.text: What warning does Jesus give about the scribes and Pharisees in Matthew 23:15?
options: They travel land and sea to make one disciple
questions.explanation: Jesus warns that they go to great lengths to make converts, but ultimately their influence leads people astray (Matthew 23:15).

questions.text: How does Jesus describe the behavior of the leaders concerning justice, mercy, and faith in Matthew 23?
questions.explanation: Jesus criticizes the leaders for neglecting the more important matters of justice, mercy, and faith while focusing on external rules (Matthew 23:23).

questions.text: What does Jesus say about the fulfillment of the prophets' messages in Matthew 23?
questions.explanation: Jesus indicates that many of the prophets' messages and warnings are fulfilled through his ministry and the events he predicts (Matthew 23:29-36).

questions.text: What is Jesus’ overall tone in Matthew 23?
questions.explanation: Throughout Matthew 23, Jesus rebukes the religious leaders sharply, warning against their hypocrisy and guiding followers away from their influences.

questions.text: What event do the disciples ask Jesus about in Matthew 24?
options: His second coming and the end of the world
questions.explanation: The disciples ask Jesus about the signs of His coming and the end of the age in Matthew 24:3, focusing on future events relating to His return.

questions.text: According to Matthew 24, what will be a sign of the end times?
options: The appearance of a new star
questions.explanation: Matthew 24:4-5 warns about false Christ and false prophets who will deceive many, indicating one of the signs of the end times.

questions.text: What did Jesus say would happen to those who endure until the end?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 24:13, Jesus states, 'The one who endures to the end will be saved,' emphasizing perseverance in faith as essential.

questions.text: How did Jesus describe the days of the coming of the Son of Man?
options: As a quiet and peaceful time
As days of great tribulation, like in Noah's time
As a time of technological advancement
questions.explanation: Matthew 24:21 compares the period of His return to the days of Noah, indicating it will be a time of great tribulation and chaos.

questions.text: What analogy does Jesus use to describe His coming in Matthew 24?
options: A shepherd returning for His sheep
questions.explanation: In Matthew 24:43-44, Jesus compares His coming to 'a thief in the night,' emphasizing the need to be watchful and prepared.

questions.text: What does Jesus say about the timing of His return in Matthew 24?
options: It will be after the world grows cold
No one knows the day or hour, only the Father
It will happen during the Feast of Tabernacles
It will be announced by angels
questions.explanation: Matthew 24:36 states, 'But about that day or hour no one knows,' emphasizing the unknowable timing of Jesus' return.

questions.text: What is the main instruction Jesus gives at the end of Matthew 24?
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes being watchful and prepared in Matthew 24:42, as His return will be sudden and unexpected.

questions.text: What should believers do regarding the gospel, according to Matthew 24:14?
options: Preach to only their local community
Keep it secret until the end
Proclaim it to all nations as a testimony
questions.explanation: Matthew 24:14 states that the gospel of the kingdom will be preached in the whole world as a testimony before the end comes, highlighting the importance of evangelism.

questions.text: In the parable of the ten virgins, what do the virgins represent?
options: Members of the church awaiting Christ's return
Disciples waiting for Jesus to start teaching
questions.explanation: The ten virgins represent members of the church or believers awaiting Christ's return, emphasizing preparedness for His coming (Matthew 25:1-13).

questions.text: What was the main reason the foolish virgins were unprepared?
options: They did not bring extra oil
questions.explanation: The foolish virgins failed to bring extra oil for their lamps, which was essential to keep their lamps burning while waiting (Matthew 25:3-4).

questions.text: In the parable of the talents, what did the servants do with the money they received?
questions.explanation: The servants invested the talents they received and gained profits, showing faithfulness and initiative (Matthew 25:16-18).

questions.text: According to the parable of the talents, what was the consequence for the servant who buried his talent?
options: He was rebuked and had his talent taken away
questions.explanation: The servant who buried his talent was rebuked for neglecting his responsibility and had his talent taken away and given to the productive servant (Matthew 25:24-30).

questions.text: What is the primary message of the judgment scene in Matthew 25:31-46?
options: People will be judged based on their faith alone
Humans are judged by caring for others
Only religious leaders will be judged
Judgment is based on acknowledging Jesus publicly
questions.explanation: The judgment emphasizes caring for others—feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, visiting prisoners—as key marks of true discipleship (Matthew 25:35-40).

questions.text: Who will be surprised by their exclusion from the kingdom in Matthew 25:41?
questions.explanation: The wicked will be surprised and condemned, as they failed to serve others, illustrating that actions reflect true faith (Matthew 25:41-43).

questions.text: What does Jesus say will happen to those who are prepared when He comes?
options: They will be rewarded with eternal life
They will receive a new home
They will be invited to a feast
They will find treasures in heaven
questions.explanation: Preparedness and faithful service lead to being rewarded with eternal life in the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 25:34).

questions.text: In Matthew 25, what is the key characteristic of the wise virgins?
options: They were vigilant and had oil ready
They arrived late to the wedding
questions.explanation: The wise virgins were vigilant and prepared with oil, symbolizing readiness for Christ’s return (Matthew 25:4).

questions.text: What event does Jesus predict will happen in Matthew 26?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 26:2, Jesus tells his disciples that after two days, the Passover will be celebrated, and he will be betrayed, predicting Judas's betrayal.

questions.text: Where does the anointing at Bethany take place in Matthew 26?
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:6-7 describes Jesus being anointed by a woman in the house of Simon the leper in Bethany, an act of devotion.

questions.text: What does Judas Iscariot plan to do in Matthew 26?
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:14-16 details Judas’s agreement to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, plotting to hand him over to the authorities.

questions.text: What special event does Jesus institute during the Last Supper in Matthew 26?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 26:26-28, Jesus takes bread and wine, establishing the tradition of communion as a remembrance of his sacrifice.

questions.text: How do Jesus’ disciples respond after he predicts his arrest in Matthew 26?
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:40-41 recounts Jesus finding his disciples asleep in the Garden of Gethsemane when he asks them to stay awake and pray.

questions.text: Who draws a sword during Jesus’ arrest in Matthew 26?
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:51-52 describes Peter drawing his sword and cutting off the servant’s ear during Jesus’ arrest, but Jesus rebukes him for violence.

questions.text: What does Jesus predict about Peter’s actions before the rooster crows?
options: Peter will deny him three times
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:34 and 26:75 contain Jesus’ prophecy that Peter will deny him three times before the rooster crows, which Peter later does.

questions.text: Who betrayed Jesus to the Roman authorities in Matthew 27?
questions.explanation: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, leading to His arrest (Matthew 27:3-4).

questions.text: What was Pilate's initial response to Jesus' claim of kingship?
options: He questioned Jesus about His kingdom
He handed Jesus over to Herod
questions.explanation: Pilate asked Jesus if He was the King of the Jews, indicating he questioned the claim (Matthew 27:11-13).

questions.text: What did the crowd choose to be released instead of Jesus?
questions.explanation: The crowd requested the release of Barabbas instead of Jesus (Matthew 27:15-26).

questions.text: How did Jesus respond when the soldiers mocked Him and placed a crown on His head?
questions.explanation: Jesus remained silent during His mockery, fulfilling prophecy (Matthew 27:27-31).

questions.text: What sign was above Jesus while He was crucified?
options: Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews
questions.explanation: The inscription read, 'Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews' (Matthew 27:37).

questions.text: What did Jesus cry out before His death, indicating fulfillment?
options: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
Father, into your hands I commit my spirit
questions.explanation: Jesus' final words were a cry of surrender: 'Father, into your hands I commit my spirit' (Matthew 27:50-51).

questions.text: What event occurred at Jesus' death according to Matthew 27?
options: The veil of the temple tore
questions.explanation: At Jesus’ death, the veil of the temple tore from top to bottom, symbolizing access to God (Matthew 27:51).

questions.text: How was Jesus buried after His death?
questions.explanation: Joseph of Arimathea provided his own tomb for Jesus’ burial, fulfilling prophecy (Matthew 27:57-60).

questions.text: Who arrived at the tomb first on the morning of Jesus' resurrection?
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene arrived first at the tomb early in the morning, as described in Matthew 28:1-2.

questions.text: What was the angel's message to the women at the tomb?
options: He has risen from the dead
questions.explanation: The angel told the women that Jesus had risen from the dead, which is the core message of Matthew 28:5-6.

questions.text: How did the guards react when the angel appeared?
options: They saw the angel and stayed alert
They fell into fear and became like dead men
questions.explanation: The guards were so afraid that they became like dead men, as described in Matthew 28:4 and 28:4-5.

questions.text: What command did the angel give to the women regarding Jesus' followers?
options: Tell the disciples to meet Jesus in Galilee
Hide the news of the resurrection
Go to the temple and report
questions.explanation: The angel instructed the women to inform the disciples to go to Galilee, where they would see Jesus again (Matthew 28:7).

questions.text: How did the women respond after being told to share the news?
options: They hurried away to tell the disciples
questions.explanation: The women quickly left the tomb to share the news with the disciples, as noted in Matthew 28:8.

questions.text: What did the risen Jesus say to the women as they went to tell the disciples?
questions.explanation: Jesus told the women to tell his brothers that He was risen, as recorded in Matthew 28:10.

questions.text: What was the main commission Jesus gave to the disciples at the end of Matthew 28?
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded the disciples to go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them and teaching them, as in Matthew 28:19-20.

questions.text: Who is described as in the wilderness in Matthew 3:1?
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:1 introduces John the Baptist as the one preaching in the wilderness of Judea, calling people to repentance.

questions.text: What message did John the Baptist preach according to Matthew 3?
options: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:2 records John calling people to repent because the kingdom of heaven is near, emphasizing preparation for God's reign.

questions.text: Which Old Testament prophet is mentioned in Matthew 3:3 as fulfilling prophecy?
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:3 cites Isaiah's prophecy about a voice crying out in the wilderness preparing the way for the Lord.

questions.text: What did John the Baptist wear according to Matthew 3:4?
options: Camel's hair with a leather belt
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:4 describes John's attire as camel's hair and a leather belt, emphasizing his ascetic lifestyle.

questions.text: Where did Jesus go after His baptism?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:1, Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness after His baptism, to be tempted by Satan.

questions.text: Who tempted Jesus in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:3 explicitly states that Satan came to tempt Jesus during His time in the wilderness.

questions.text: What was Jesus' response when tempted to turn stones into bread?
options: It is written, man shall not live by bread alone
I will do it if it is God's will
questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:4, Jesus responded to Satan by quoting Scripture: 'It is written, man shall not live by bread alone,' emphasizing reliance on God's word.

questions.text: To whom did Satan show all the kingdoms of the world?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:8-9 records Satan showing Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and offering them if He would worship him.

questions.text: What command does Satan give Jesus at the pinnacle of the temple?
options: Jump and let angels catch you
questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:5-6, Satan tempts Jesus to jump from the temple pinnacle, quoting Scripture and urging Jesus to trust God's angels to protect Him.

questions.text: How does Jesus respond to Satan's temptations?
questions.explanation: Throughout Matthew 4, Jesus responds to each temptation by quoting Scripture, showing reliance on God's word to resist Satan.

questions.text: What is the ultimate command Jesus gives for resisting temptation?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:10, Jesus commands Satan to depart, affirming that worship and service should be directed only to God.

questions.text: What was the outcome of Jesus' time in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:11 states that afterward, angels came to minister to Jesus, indicating victory and divine support after resisting temptation.

questions.text: What is Jesus doing in Matthew 5:1 that leads to the Sermon on the Mount?
options: Sitting on a mountain and teaching
questions.explanation: Jesus is depicted sitting on a mountain as He begins to teach His disciples, which is the setting for the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:1).

questions.text: Which group is Jesus primarily addressing in the Beatitudes?
questions.explanation: Jesus primarily teaches His disciples, guiding them on how to live as His followers (Matthew 5:1-2).

questions.text: What does Jesus say about the peacemakers in Matthew 5:9?
options: They will be called God’s children
They will be rewarded in heaven
questions.explanation: Jesus states that peacemakers are called 'children of God' (Matthew 5:9), emphasizing their special status in God's kingdom.

questions.text: According to Matthew 5, how should followers of Jesus view the law?
options: They should fulfill and uphold it
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that he came to fulfill the law and that His followers should uphold it, not abolish it (Matthew 5:17-19).

questions.text: What does Jesus say about anger in Matthew 5:22?
options: It's acceptable if you're not angry with others
It's equivalent to murder in the heart
It can be justified in certain situations
questions.explanation: Jesus equates anger with murder in the heart, emphasizing the importance of reconciliation and purity of heart (Matthew 5:22).

questions.text: In Matthew 5, Jesus teaches that righteousness should surpass which group's righteousness?
questions.explanation: Jesus explains that His followers' righteousness must surpass that of the Pharisees to enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 5:20).

questions.text: What does Jesus say about loving enemies in Matthew 5:44?
options: Pray for those who persecute you
questions.explanation: Jesus instructs His followers to love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them, exemplifying divine love (Matthew 5:44).

questions.text: In Matthew 5, what advice does Jesus give about giving to the needy?
options: Give only if it benefits you
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that giving should be done in secret, not for show, to be pleasing to God (Matthew 5:3).

questions.text: According to Matthew 6, what should be done in secret rather than publicly to seek God's reward?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6 emphasizes that giving to the needy should be done secretly, not for public recognition (verse 3-4).

questions.text: What example does Jesus give to illustrate the importance of prayer in Matthew 6?
options: The parable of the prodigal son
questions.explanation: Jesus provides the Lord’s Prayer as a model for prayer, emphasizing sincerity over repetition (verses 9-13).

questions.text: In Matthew 6, Jesus warns against practicing righteousness for what purpose?
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that acts of righteousness should not be done to seek human recognition, but for God's approval (verse 1).

questions.text: What does Matthew 6 say about storing treasures on earth vs. in heaven?
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that treasures in heaven are lasting and not subject to decay or theft (verse 19-20).

questions.text: How does Jesus instruct us to handle worry about material needs in Matthew 6?
questions.explanation: Jesus encourages seeking God's kingdom first, trusting that God will provide for our needs (verse 33).

questions.text: In Matthew 6, what is Jesus' teaching about judging others?
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches not to judge others lest we be judged ourselves, emphasizing humility and self-examination (verse 1-4).

questions.text: What does Matthew 6 suggest about fasting and how it should be done?
options: Fasting should be done in secret
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes that fasting should be kept secret, not used to gain human praise (verse 16-18).

questions.text: What is the main theme of Matthew 6?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6 focuses on practicing righteousness with sincerity, prioritizing God's kingdom over worldly concerns, illustrating Kingdom principles.

questions.text: According to Matthew 7:1, what are believers advised not to do?
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:1 states, 'Judge not, that ye be not judged,' emphasizing that we should avoid condemning others unfairly. This verse highlights the importance of humility and restraint in judgment.

questions.text: What does Jesus say about the measurement used for judging in Matthew 7:2?
options: It will be measured to you
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:2 explains that the way you judge others will be the standard used to judge you, illustrating the principle of reciprocal judgment.

questions.text: In Matthew 7:3-5, what is Jesus cautioning against?
options: Pointing out other's faults while ignoring one's own
questions.explanation: Jesus addresses the hypocrisy of noticing the speck in another’s eye while ignoring the plank in one’s own eye, warning against self-righteous judgment.

questions.text: According to Matthew 7:7-8, what should believers do to receive, find, and have questions answered?
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:7-8 encourages believers to ask, seek, and knock, promising that they will receive, find, and have doors opened for them.

questions.text: What does Matthew 7:12 state about how we should treat others?
options: Do unto others as you would have them do unto you
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:12 summarizes the Golden Rule: to treat others as you would like to be treated, a central ethical teaching of Jesus.

questions.text: In Matthew 7:15-20, what does Jesus warn about false prophets?
options: They come in sheep’s clothing but are inwardly ravenous wolves
questions.explanation: Jesus warns that false prophets appear harmless outwardly but are inwardly destructive, and their true character can be identified by their fruits.

questions.text: What does the analogy of the two builders in Matthew 7:24-27 illustrate?
options: Building on the rock leads to stability
Building is a metaphor for patience
questions.explanation: Jesus compares those who hear His words and act on them to a wise builder who builds on the rock, illustrating the importance of obedience for stability and foundation.

questions.text: What notable act does Jesus perform in Matthew 8:2-3?
options: He heals a man with leprosy
He calms a storm at sea
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:2-3, Jesus heals a man with leprosy, demonstrating His authority over illness and impurity.

questions.text: How does Jesus respond to the faith of the centurion in Matthew 8:8-10?
options: He heals his servant because of his faith
He directs the centurion to the synagogue
He tells him to wait and see
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:8-10, Jesus commends the centurion’s great faith and heals his servant as a result.

questions.text: What does Jesus do to the storm on the Sea of Galilee in Matthew 8:23-27?
options: He commands it to be still
He walks on water to calm it
He rebukes the disciples for fear
He sends a boat to dock
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:23-27, Jesus calms the storm by commanding it to be still, demonstrating His power over nature.

questions.text: How does the healed man from the demon-possessed region respond in Matthew 8:28-34?
options: He follows Jesus to his hometown
He refuses to speak about Jesus
He offers sacrifices at the synagogue
He wants to stay in the tombs
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:28-34, the man who was possessed asks to go with Jesus, but Jesus instructs him to share what God has done for him locally.

questions.text: What does Jesus say about following Him in Matthew 8:19-20?
options: Foxes have holes, birds have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to rest
Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men
The first will be last, and the last first
Let the dead bury their dead
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:20, Jesus comments on the difficulty of truly following Him, noting that He has no permanent earthly dwelling.

questions.text: What command does Jesus give when healing Peter’s mother-in-law in Matthew 8:14-15?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:14-15, Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law, and she immediately begins to serve them, showing her gratitude.

questions.text: What response do the crowds have to Jesus' miracles in Matthew 8?
options: They are amazed and praise God
questions.explanation: Throughout Matthew 8, the crowds are amazed by Jesus’ miracles and praise God for His power and compassion.

questions.text: What did Jesus do after crossing the sea in Matthew 9:1?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:2, Jesus heals a paralytic after crossing the sea, demonstrating His authority to forgive sins and heal.

questions.text: How did the friends of the paralytic demonstrate their faith?
options: By bringing him to Jesus and lowering him through the roof
questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:2-6, their faith is shown by bringing the paralytic to Jesus and lowering him through the roof so Jesus could heal him.

questions.text: What was Jesus’ response to the crowd when He said the paralytic's sins were forgiven?
options: He explained that only God can forgive sins
questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:3-4, Jesus perceives their thoughts and asserts that forgiveness of sins is within His authority, which surprised the crowd.

questions.text: What was the reason Jesus later gave for eating with tax collectors and sinners?
options: He came to call sinners to repentance
questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:13, Jesus states He came to call sinners, not the righteous, to repentance, emphasizing His mission.

questions.text: Who questioned Jesus about fasting?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:14, the disciples of John asked Jesus why His disciples did not fast, contrasting with the Pharisees' practices.

questions.text: What analogy does Jesus use to explain why His disciples do not fast?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:15, Jesus compares His time with His disciples to a wedding feast, implying joy during His presence.

questions.text: What miracle does Jesus perform in Matthew 9:20-22?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:20-22, Jesus heals a woman who had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years.

questions.text: What was the reason the woman with bleeding touched Jesus’ cloak?
options: She believed she would be healed by faith
questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:21, her faith believed that touching Jesus’ cloak would bring healing, which it did.

questions.text: Who was the prophet that received the vision in Micah 1?
questions.explanation: Micah is the prophet who received the vision recorded in Micah 1:1, as introduced in the opening verse.

questions.text: From which city does Micah originate?
questions.explanation: Micah 1:1 mentions Moresheth as the hometown of Micah, located in Judah.

questions.text: What is the main theme introduced at the start of Micah 1?
questions.explanation: Micah 1 opens with a vision of judgment against Israel and surrounding nations, emphasizing downfall due to sin.

questions.text: Which natural feature is used poetically to describe the coming judgment?
questions.explanation: Micah 1:3 describes the Lord coming from His dwelling, causing the earth to tremble and mountains to melt, symbolizing divine judgment.

questions.text: What specific city is mentioned as being affected by the judgment?
questions.explanation: Micah 1:5 specifically mentions Samaria as one of the cities bearing the blame for Israel’s sins.

questions.text: In Micah 1, what reasons are given for God’s coming judgment?
questions.explanation: The chapter highlights Israel’s sins such as idol worship and social injustice as reasons for God's judgment (Micah 1:7).

questions.text: How does Micah describe the fall of cities like Bethphage and Gath?
questions.explanation: Micah 1:11 describes the destruction of the cities as part of divine judgment, indicating they will be torn down.

questions.text: What do the descriptions of the coming judgment emphasize about God's character?
questions.explanation: The chapter emphasizes God's justice and holiness as He responds to Israel’s sins with judgment (Micah 1:3-5).

questions.text: What is the main behavior condemned in Micah 2:1?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:1 describes how people plot evil on their beds, highlighting their wicked plans before executing them during the day.

questions.text: According to Micah 2:3, what is God's response to these evil plans?
options: He will bring disaster upon them
questions.explanation: Micah 2:3 states that God will bring disaster upon those who devise evil plans, as a consequence of their wickedness.

questions.text: What does Micah 2:5 say about the inheritance of those who take property unjustly?
options: They will scatter it among the poor
They will have no one to cast lots for their land
They will be given more land
questions.explanation: Micah 2:5 mentions that those who seize land unjustly will find no one to cast lots for their inheritance, implying loss and injustice correction.

questions.text: How are the rebellious women described in Micah 2:9?
options: They are driven from their homes
questions.explanation: Micah 2:9 describes rebellious women being driven out of their homes because of the injustice and unrighteousness in the land.

questions.text: What does Micah 2:12-13 promise regarding God's people?
options: They will be led out and gathered
They will establish their own kings
questions.explanation: Micah 2:12-13 speaks of God's promise to gather His people, led by a shepherd who opens the way for them out of captivity.

questions.text: In Micah 2:7, what is God's attitude toward the prophets who lead people astray?
options: They will be judged for their falsehood
questions.explanation: Micah 2:7 indicates that false prophets who lead people astray will face divine judgment, as their words are not from the Lord.

questions.text: What is the overall theme of Micah 2?
questions.explanation: Micah 2 addresses God's judgment against those who plot evil, seize property unjustly, and rebel against Him, emphasizing the need for righteousness.

questions.text: What does Micah 2:10 instruct God's people to do?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:10 urges God's people to flee from the unclean land because it will be desolate and unsuitable for habitation.

questions.text: What group does Micah accuse of oppressing the people in Micah 3?
questions.explanation: Micah 3 condemns rulers, princes, and officials for oppressing the people unjustly (verses 1-3).

questions.text: According to Micah 3, how do the rulers and prophets speak?
questions.explanation: Micah 3 describes them as speaking lies and falsehoods to deceive the people (verses 5-7).

questions.text: What consequence does Micah warn will happen to Jerusalem because of the leaders' corruption?
options: It will become a nation of prophets
questions.explanation: Micah warns that Jerusalem will be made a heap of ruins because of the corrupt leaders (verse 12).

questions.text: In Micah 3, who does God promise will be among the leaders in the future?
questions.explanation: Micah indicates that in the future, rulers will seek justice and righteousness, implying a hope for righteous leadership (verse 9-11).

questions.text: What does Micah say will happen to the prophets who lead people astray?
options: They will be removed from the land
They will be disgraced by God
questions.explanation: Micah proclaims that false prophets who lead people astray will face disgrace from God, and their visions will be exposed (verse 5).

questions.text: According to Micah 3, what motivated the rulers and prophets' wrongful acts?
questions.explanation: Their actions are driven by greed and desire for personal gain at the expense of justice (verses 2-3, 11).

questions.text: What metaphor does Micah use to describe Jerusalem's future in verse 12?
questions.explanation: Micah describes Jerusalem as a heap of ruins because of the corruption and judgment upon it (verse 12).

questions.text: In Micah 4, what is predicted about the mountain of the Lord?
options: It will be established as the highest mountain
It will be consumed by fire
It will be made into a plain
It will be hidden from sight
questions.explanation: Micah 4:1 describes how the mountain of the Lord will be established as the highest and will attract peoples from many nations.

questions.text: According to Micah 4, what will happen to nations that arm themselves for war?
options: They will be blessed by God
They will be broken and beaten down
questions.explanation: Micah 4:3 states that God will bring peace and break down weapons of war, turning swords into plowshares.

questions.text: What is said about the future location of Israel’s people in Micah 4?
options: They will dwell safely and securely in their land
They will migrate to distant lands
They will exile to Babylon again
questions.explanation: Micah 4:4 describes Israel’s people dwelling safely, with no one making them afraid, indicating peace and security in their land.

questions.text: What is the focus of Micah 4:5 regarding nations?
options: All nations will seek their own way
All nations will serve the Lord
questions.explanation: Micah 4:5 emphasizes that many nations will follow the Lord and seek His name, highlighting unity under God's sovereignty.

questions.text: In Micah 4, who is described as gathering the people of Israel?
questions.explanation: God is depicted as the one who gathers and restores the scattered Israelites in Micah 4.

questions.text: What ancient city is referred to as a fortified city in Micah 4:8?
questions.explanation: Micah 4:8 mentions Zion as a stronghold and the seat of God's reign, even as it is restored.

questions.text: What will happen to the nations that previously gathered against Israel, according to Micah 4?
options: They will be defeated and turned to destruction
They will join Israel in worshiping the Lord
They will be expelled from the land
They will establish peace among themselves
questions.explanation: Micah 4:11-13 describes how many nations will come against Israel and be defeated, with God executing judgment on them.

questions.text: What is the primary message of Micah 4 about the future from God's perspective?
options: Peace and divine rule will be established over the earth
questions.explanation: Micah 4 focuses on God's plan to establish peace, divine rule, and restoration of Israel in the last days.

questions.text: According to Micah 5:1, who is the ruler's origin described as?
questions.explanation: Micah 5:2 states that the ruler's origin is from Bethlehem Ephrathah, emphasizing the prophecy of a ruler coming from that small town.

questions.text: What will happen to the remnant of Jacob according to Micah 5:7?
options: They will be a mighty nation
questions.explanation: Micah 5:7 describes how the remnant of Jacob will become a mighty nation and a blessing amidst many peoples.

questions.text: In Micah 6, what does God ask His people to do instead of offering empty sacrifices?
questions.explanation: Micah 6 emphasizes that God desires justice, kindness, and humility over empty sacrifices (Micah 6:6-8).

questions.text: According to Micah 6, what is considered the Lord's answer to His people's accusations?
